content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 19, ¶p0133).**

Section 19 binds Sparkling Spring Water Group as well as Garman, and it is a **no-hire**, not a non-solicit — "both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire." Its first limb sweeps in *any* employee of the other party with no link to the engagement; the "directly involved in the provision of services" qualifier attaches only to the second, former-employee limb. There is also no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. A no-hire covering all personnel is walk-away territory under NOSOLICIT, so the clause fails the fallback despite being mutual and only one year long.

The validated redline (fallback level, given the mutual bargain) makes the minimum changes: solicitation only, 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, express carve-outs for general advertising and self-initiated approaches, and no-hire deleted. Survival of Section 19 under Section 18 is acceptable once the covenant is narrowed.
